Course 03 · Undergraduate, with graduate extensions
Calculus
Single- and multivariable calculus with rigorous foundations, optimization and dynamics for economics and statistics.

Readings

Readings are listed by session. Core textbooks for the whole course are listed at the end.

Lecture 1: Limits, Continuity, and the Logic of Analysis

Apostol, Calculus, Vol. 1; Spivak, Calculus; Rudin, Principles of Mathematical Analysis.

Lecture 2: Sequences, Convergence, and Infinite Series

Apostol, Calculus, Vol. 1; Spivak, Calculus; Rudin, Principles of Mathematical Analysis.

Lecture 3: Differentiation, Mean Value Theorems, and Comparative Rates

Apostol, Calculus, Vol. 1; Chiang and Wainwright, Fundamental Methods of Mathematical Economics; Simon and Blume, Mathematics for Economists.

Lecture 4: Taylor Approximation, Convexity, and Single-Variable Optimization

Apostol, Calculus, Vol. 1; Chiang and Wainwright, Fundamental Methods of Mathematical Economics; Simon and Blume, Mathematics for Economists.

Lecture 5: Integration, Riemann Sums, and the Fundamental Theorem

Apostol, Calculus, Vol. 1; Spivak, Calculus; Chiang and Wainwright, Fundamental Methods of Mathematical Economics.

Lecture 6: Multivariable Functions, Limits, and Continuity

Apostol, Calculus, Vol. 2; Simon and Blume, Mathematics for Economists; Chiang and Wainwright, Fundamental Methods of Mathematical Economics.

Lecture 7: Partial Derivatives, Total Differentials, and the Chain Rule

Apostol, Calculus, Vol. 2; Simon and Blume, Mathematics for Economists; Chiang and Wainwright, Fundamental Methods of Mathematical Economics.

Lecture 8: Hessians and Unconstrained Multivariable Optimization

Simon and Blume, Mathematics for Economists; Sundaram, A First Course in Optimization Theory; Apostol, Calculus, Vol. 2.

Lecture 9: Equality Constraints and Lagrange Multipliers

Sundaram, A First Course in Optimization Theory; Chiang and Wainwright, Fundamental Methods of Mathematical Economics; Simon and Blume, Mathematics for Economists.

Lecture 10: Inequality Constraints and Karush–Kuhn–Tucker Conditions

Sundaram, A First Course in Optimization Theory; Nocedal and Wright, Numerical Optimization; Chiang and Wainwright, Fundamental Methods of Mathematical Economics.

Lecture 11: Implicit and Inverse Function Theorems

Simon and Blume, Mathematics for Economists; Chiang and Wainwright, Fundamental Methods of Mathematical Economics; Apostol, Calculus, Vol. 2.

Lecture 12: Multiple Integrals, Change of Variables, and Probability

Apostol, Calculus, Vol. 2; Casella and Berger, Statistical Inference; Simon and Blume, Mathematics for Economists.

Lecture 13: Differential Equations and Continuous-Time Dynamics

Boyce, DiPrima, and Meade, Elementary Differential Equations; Chiang and Wainwright, Fundamental Methods of Mathematical Economics; Strogatz, Nonlinear Dynamics and Chaos.

Lecture 14: Difference Equations and Discrete-Time Dynamics

Chiang and Wainwright, Fundamental Methods of Mathematical Economics; Simon and Blume, Mathematics for Economists; Strogatz, Nonlinear Dynamics and Chaos.

Core textbooks

  • Apostol, Calculus, Volumes 1 and 2.
  • Spivak, Calculus.
  • Simon and Blume, Mathematics for Economists.
  • Chiang and Wainwright, Fundamental Methods of Mathematical Economics.
  • Rudin, Principles of Mathematical Analysis (selected advanced topics).
